title: Integrality criterion for a monomial
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $P$ a submonoid of an abelian group $G$, and $g\in G$, using additive monoid notation as in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. For a submonoid $Q\subseteq G$, write $k[Q]=\bigoplus_{q\in Q}ke^q\subseteq k[G]$, with $e^qe^{q'}=e^{q+q'}$ and identity $e^0$. Thus its elements are finite sums of these basis monomials. Put $P^{\mathrm{sat}}=\{h\in G:\exists n\geq1,\ nh\in P\}$, with saturation here taken in the specified ambient group $G$. In $k[G]$, the monomial $e^g$ is integral over the subalgebra $k[P]$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] if and only if there exists an integer $n>0$ with $ng\in P$. Consequently, for every such $P$, the subalgebra $k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ is integral over $k[P]$, meaning that each of its elements is integral over $k[P]$. No finite-generation or torsion-freeness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and the monomial-basis normalization argument, printed p.104

proof.text: Suppose $e^g$ is integral over $k[P]$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] there are $d\geq1$ and $a_i\in k[P]$ for $0\leq i<d$ such that $e^{dg}+\sum_{i<d}a_i e^{ig}=0$. For $h\in G$, denote the coefficient of $e^h$ in $a_i$ by $c_i(h)$; it is zero when $h\notin P$. Multiplication by $e^{ig}$ shifts the basis index by $ig$, so the coefficient of $e^{dg}$ in this equation is $1+\sum_{i<d}c_i((d-i)g)=0$ in $k$. If every $(d-i)g$ were outside $P$, the sum would vanish and give $1=0$, contrary to $k$ being a field. Hence for some $i<d$, $n=d-i>0$ satisfies $ng\in P$. This coefficient calculation only uses cancellation in the group $G$; distinct powers of $g$ need not be distinct.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17 and Lemma 3.2.9, printed pp.101,104: supporting algebraic lemma; direct monomial-coefficient argument supplied by the worker, not a quotation of the source proof.

proof.text: Conversely, if $n\geq1$ and $ng\in P$, the polynomial $T^n-e^{ng}\in k[P][T]$ is monic of degree $n$ and vanishes at $e^g$, since $(e^g)^n=e^{ng}$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] this is exactly integrality of $e^g$ over $k[P]$. Together with Step 1 this proves the equivalence.

proof.text: The set $Q=P^{\mathrm{sat}}$ is a submonoid containing $P$: $0\in Q$, and if $ah,bh'\in P$ for positive $a,b$, then $ab(h+h')=b(ah)+a(bh')\in P$. Every $h\in Q$ has $nh\in P$ for some $n\geq1$, so Step 2 makes $e^h$ integral over $R=k[P]$. Apply [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] to the inclusion $R\hookrightarrow k[G]$: its statement says that the set $C$ of integral elements is a subring containing $R$. Every scalar $c e^0$ lies in $R$, hence in $C$; thus each $c e^h=(c e^0)e^h$ lies in $C$. Each element of $k[Q]$ is a finite sum of such terms, and repeated closure under addition (starting from $0\in C$ for the empty sum) puts it in $C$. Consequently every element of $k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ is integral over $k[P]$, as asserted.
